metadata.remarks: The Security Operations composite defines the operational authority and governance layer that binds security telemetry, monitoring, detection, response, forensics, and automation. This composite does not generate signals, perform analytics, or execute forensic analysis. Its role is to ensure that decisions, escalation, and automation occur under explicit authority and preserve evidentiary and governance integrity.

components.title: Security Operations Authority and Roles
components.description: Definition of operational authority, role separation, and decision ownership across SecOps functions.
components.remarks: This component exists to prevent tool-driven authority drift and ensure accountability for security decisions.

components.title: Operational Workflow and Escalation Control
components.description: Definition of approved workflows from detection to incident to investigation, including escalation thresholds and governance handoff.
components.remarks: Ensures that detections do not silently normalize into acceptable states and that violations escalate appropriately.

components.title: Automation and SOAR Governance
components.description: Constraints governing where automation may be used and what actions may be executed without human approval.
components.remarks: This component explicitly bounds SOAR to pre-approved, reversible actions and forbids autonomous decision-making.

components.title: Evidence Preservation and Coordination
components.description: Operational safeguards ensuring that response and automation do not destroy or contaminate forensic evidence.
components.remarks: Ensures clean handoff to Digital Forensics and preserves legal and investigative integrity.

components.title: SecOps Pattern Binding
components.description: Explicit binding of Logging & Telemetry, Security Monitoring, Threat Detection, Incident Response, and Digital Forensics under a unified operational authority.
components.remarks: Prevents collapse of responsibilities across base patterns while enabling coordinated operations.
